title: Amex 2022 10-K — Critical Accounting Estimates: Liability for Membership Rewards (URR and WAC per point, sensitivity)
url: kb_demo/financebench/pdfs/AMERICANEXPRESS_2022_10K.pdf · p83 (Critical Accounting Estimates — Liability for Membership Rewards)
key_points: The Membership Rewards liability is estimated to cover the cost of all points previously earned but not yet redeemed by current enrollees as of the end of the reporting period.
Two key assumptions drive the estimate: the Ultimate Redemption Rate (URR) and the weighted average cost (WAC) per point.
A 25 basis point increase in the estimated URR of current enrollees would increase the Membership Rewards liability and rewards expense by approximately $157 million.
A 1 basis point increase in the WAC per point would increase the Membership Rewards liability and rewards expense by approximately $190 million.
Amex periodically evaluates its liability estimation process and assumptions based on developments in redemption patterns, cost per point redeemed, partner contract changes and other factors.
Estimating the Membership Rewards liability involves a high degree of judgment; actual redemptions and costs could differ significantly from estimates.
raw_excerpt: Changes in the Membership Rewards URR and WAC per point have the effect of either increasing or decreasing the liability through the current period Membership Rewards expense by an amount estimated to cover the cost of all points previously earned but not yet redeemed by current enrollees as of the end of the reporting period. As of December 31, 2022, an increase in the estimated URR of current enrollees of 25 basis points would increase the Membership Rewards liability and corresponding rewards expense by approximately $157 million. Similarly, an increase in the WAC per point of 1 basis point would increase the Membership Rewards liability and corresponding rewards expense by approximately $190 million.

title: Amex 2022 10-K — Critical Accounting Estimates: CECL methodology effective January 1, 2020
key_points: The CECL methodology became effective January 1, 2020.

CECL requires Amex to estimate lifetime expected credit losses by incorporating historical loss experience and current and future economic conditions over a reasonable and supportable period beyond the balance sheet date.
CECL governs reserves on Card Member loans and receivables (contra-asset accounts), not the measurement of liability captions.
Amex refers readers to Note 1 for a summary of significant accounting policies and identifies certain policies as requiring critical estimates.
raw_excerpt: The CECL methodology, which became effective January 1, 2020, requires us to estimate lifetime expected credit losses by incorporating historical loss experience, as well as current and future economic conditions over a reasonable and supportable period (R&S Period) beyond the balance sheet date.

title: American Express 2022 10-K — MD&A Deposit Programs (AENB direct retail deposits as primary channel)
key_points: Deposits are offered within U.S. bank subsidiary American Express National Bank (AENB) and are FDIC-insured up to at least $250,000 per account holder.

Management states that direct retail deposits offered by AENB is its primary deposit product channel, making FDIC-insured high-yield savings account and certificates of deposit (CDs) products available directly to consumers.
AENB also offers checking account products and sources deposits through third-party distribution channels as needed to meet overall funding objectives.
Management states the company had $110.2 billion in deposits as of December 31, 2022.
Management notes that the ability to obtain deposit funding and offer competitive interest rates depends on, among other factors, the capital level of AENB.
raw_excerpt:
DEPOSIT PROGRAMS
We offer deposits within our U.S. bank subsidiary, AENB. These funds are currently insured up to an amount that is at least $250,000 per account holder through the FDIC. Our ability to obtain deposit funding and offer competitive interest rates is dependent on, among other factors, the capital level of AENB.
Direct retail deposits offered by AENB is our primary deposit product channel, which makes FDIC-insured high-yield savings account and certificates of deposit (CDs) products available directly to consumers. AENB also offers checking account products and sources deposits through third-party distribution channels as needed to meet our overall funding objectives. As of December 31, 2022, we had $110.2 billion in deposits.
